reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the formation of a protective, adherent Al2O3 layer and reduced oxidation in fluorine-treated Ti-45Al-8.5Nb, but it provides no data on mechanical properties or on HfNbTaTiZr, so the premise that mechanical performance is uncompromised is unsupported, and the transferability to the HEA is assumed.
premises: Fluorine treatment promotes formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 protective layer on Ti–Al–Nb alloys at 1000 °C
The Al2O3 layer significantly reduces oxidation weight gain in Ti–Al–Nb alloys
The Al2O3 layer adheres strongly to the substrate
The fluorine effect can be achieved by a simple spraying process with NH4F solution
The treatment leaves the bulk microstructure intact and does not compromise mechanical performance
